nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$, $l$ and $k \ge 1$, the empty range $\{1, \dots, 0\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$.
nodes.title: The empty range has a sum-free partition

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $k$, $l$ and $n$, the range $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if there is a coloring $c$ of the natural numbers with $k$ colors such that, for each color $j$, the set of integers $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$ and $c(a) = j$ is $l$-sum-free modulo $m$. Classes may be empty; for $k = 0$ there is no coloring, so the property fails for every $n$,…
nodes.title: Sum-free partitions modulo $m$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $l$ be positive integers with $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$, and let $a$ be a natural number not divisible by $p^i$. Then the singleton $\{a\}$ is $l$-sum-free modulo $p^i$.
nodes.title: Singletons are sum-free modulo a prime power

nodes.summary: The singleton $\{1\}$ is $2$-sum-free modulo $3$, since $1 + 1 \not\equiv 1 \pmod{3}$.
nodes.title: $\{1\}$ is $2$-sum-free modulo $3$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$ and $l$, a set $A$ of integers is $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if there are no $x_1, \dots, x_l, y \in A$ (repetitions allowed) with $x_1 + \dots + x_l \equiv y \pmod{m}$.
nodes.title: Sum-free sets modulo $m$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $l$ be positive integers with $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$, and let $1 \le k \le p - 1$. Then the generalized Schur number $S_{p^i}(k, l)$, the largest $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $p^i$, is at least $k$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for modular Schur numbers modulo a prime power

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be integers, let $m$ be a positive integer, and let $d = \gcd(a, m)$. The congruence $a x \equiv b \pmod{m}$ has an integer solution if and only if $d \mid b$. If $d \mid b$, then exactly $d$ of the numbers $x \in \{0, 1, \dots, m - 1\}$ are solutions. Moreover, if $x_0$ is a solution, then an integer $x$ is a solution if and only if $x \equiv x_0 + u \cdot (m / d) \pmod{m}$ for some integer $u$…
nodes.title: Solutions of a linear congruence

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ be a positive integer, and let $l$ be a natural number with $l \ge p^i - 1$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$. If $a$ and $b$ are natural numbers such that $\{a, b\}$ is $l$-sum-free modulo $p^i$, then $a \equiv b \pmod{p}$.
nodes.title: Elements of a sum-free pair are congruent modulo $p$

nodes.summary: Let $l \ge 2$ and $m \ge 2$ be natural numbers such that $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{d}$ for every divisor $d \ne 1$ of $m$, and let $k \ge m - 1$. Then the generalized Schur number $S_m(k, l)$, the largest $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$, equals $m - 1$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers attaining $m - 1$

nodes.summary: Let $m$, $k$ and $l$ be positive integers. The generalized Schur number $S_m(k, l)$, the largest $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ classes that are $l$-sum-free modulo $m$, equals $0$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$.
nodes.title: Vanishing of modular Schur numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_5(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $5$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 5$, then $S_5(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_5(1, l) = 1$; if $k \in \{2, 3\}$ and $l \ne 2$, then $S_5(k, l) = k$; and if $k \in \{2, 3\}$ and $l = 2$, or if $k \ge 4$, then $S_5(k, l) = 4$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 5

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_4(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $4$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then $S_4(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise, if $k = 1$, or if $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, then $S_4(k, l) = 1$; and if $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 0$ or $2 \pmod 4$, then $S_4(k, l) = 3$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 4

nodes.summary: Let $m$, $k$, $l$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 1$, $l \ge 1$ and $1 \le a \le m - 1$, and let $d = \gcd(a, m)$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m/d}$, then the generalized Schur number $S_m(k, l)$ modulo $m$ satisfies $S_m(k, l) < a$.
nodes.title: Congruence upper bound for modular Schur numbers

nodes.summary: Let $l$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $l \ge 2$, $m \ge 2$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod m$. Then the generalized Schur number $S_m(1, l)$ modulo $m$ equals $1$ if and only if $l = 2$ or $2l \ge m + 1$.
nodes.title: When the one-class modular Schur number equals one

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $l$ be positive integers with $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$, and let $k$ be a natural number with $k \ge p^i - 1$. Then the generalized Schur number modulo $p^i$ satisfies $S_{p^i}(k, l) = p^i - 1$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo a prime power for many classes

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $l$ be a positive integer with $l \ge p - 1$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod p$. Then the generalized Schur number modulo $p$ satisfies $S_p(k, l) = k$ for every natural number $k$ with $1 \le k \le p - 1$, and $S_p(k, l) = p - 1$ for every natural number $k \ge p - 1$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo a prime

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_7(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $7$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 7$, then $S_7(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_7(k, l) = 1$ if $k = 1$ and $l \ne 3$; $S_7(k, l) = 2$ if $k = 1$ and $l = 3$, or $k = 2$ and $l \ge 4$; $S_7(k, l) = 3$ if $k = 2$ and $l \in \{2, 3\}$, or $k = 3$ and $l \ge 5$; $S_7(k, l) = 4$ if $k = 4$ and $l \ge 5$; $S_7(k, l) = 5$ if $k = 3$ and…
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 7

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_6(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $6$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, then $S_6(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_6(k, l) = 1$ if $k = 1$ and $l \ne 3$, or $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 4 \pmod 6$; $S_6(k, l) = 2$ if $k = 1$ and $l = 3$, or $k \ge 2$ and $l \equiv 3$ or $5 \pmod 6$; $S_6(k, l) = 3$ if $k = 2$, $l \equiv 0$ or $2 \pmod 6$, and $l \ge 6$; $S_6(k, l) = 4$ if…
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 6

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers and let $S_3(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $3$. If $l \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, then $S_3(k, l) = 0$. Otherwise $S_3(1, l) = 1$, and $S_3(k, l) = 2$ for every $k \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo 3

nodes.summary: Let $k$, $l$ and $n$ be natural numbers with $k \ge 2$, $n \ge 2$, $l \ge 1$ and $l \not\equiv 1 \pmod{2n}$, and let $S_{2n}(k, l)$ be the generalized Schur number modulo $2n$. If $l \equiv n + 1 \pmod{2n}$, then $S_{2n}(k, l) = 1$; otherwise $S_{2n}(k, l) \ge 2$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo an even number

nodes.summary: For all positive integers $k$ and $l$, the modular Schur number $S_2(k, l)$ equals $0$ when $l$ is odd and equals $1$ when $l$ is even.
nodes.title: Modular Schur numbers modulo $2$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $m$, $k$ and $l$, the generalized Schur number modulo $m$, written $S_m(k, l)$, is the largest natural number $n$ such that $\{1, \dots, n\}$ admits a partition into $k$ (possibly empty) classes that are each $l$-sum-free modulo $m$; it is $0$ when there is no largest such $n$.
nodes.title: Modular Schur number

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $l$ be natural numbers and let $A$ be a set of integers. If $A$ contains an integer $a$ divisible by $m$, then $A$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$: the sum of $l$ copies of $a$ is congruent to $a$ modulo $m$.
nodes.title: Sets containing a multiple of the modulus are not sum-free

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $l$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $l \ge 1$, $m \ge 1$ and $m \nmid a$, and let $d = \gcd(a, m)$. If $d = 1$, then $\{a\}$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$. If $d > 1$, then $\{a\}$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m/d}$.
nodes.title: When a singleton set is sum-free

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and $l$ be natural numbers. The singleton $\{1\}$ is not $l$-sum-free modulo $m$ if and only if $l \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$.
nodes.title: When the singleton $\{1\}$ is sum-free

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
